rfi.title: Suez Crisis at 70 reveals the humiliation France tried to keep hidden
rfi.description: Seventy years after France, the United Kingdom and Israel invaded Egypt following its nationalisation of the Suez Canal, the military operation is remembered as a diplomatic disaster. Friday marks the anniversary of a ceasefire that halted the fighting under international pressure, despite the invading forces' success on the battlefield. Archive footage excluded from French cinema newsreels shows the humiliation that followed, as Europe's colonial powers faced the limits of their influence.

rfi.title: French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters
rfi.description: Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.

rfi.title: Three-quarters of world's displaced people 'on frontlines of climate crisis'
rfi.description: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN refugee agency has said, urging action ahead of next week's Cop31 climate summit in Turkey.

rfi.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years for Shakahola forest deaths
rfi.description: A self-proclaimed preacher from Kenya was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for murdering 191 people, mostly children, by forcing them to starve to death. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult's base near the beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the Shakahola forest massacre.

rfi.title: Tanzania opposition leader Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for incitement
rfi.description: A Tanzanian court on Friday sentenced opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in jail for inciting unrest, after earlier in the day clearing him of treason – meaning he avoided a possible death sentence. The verdict follows a disputed presidential election and a deadly crackdown on protesters, in a case that has drawn international condemnation and raised concerns about political freedom in the country.

rfi.title: Uncertainty over Nigeria vote after court bars opposition leader from running

rfi.title: Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France
rfi.description: French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.

rfi.title: Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding
rfi.description: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.

rfi.title: ‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book
rfi.description: Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.

rfi.title: Unicef warns attacks on water supply in conflict zones have tripled in five years
rfi.description: Attacks damaging or destroying water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, Unicef warned on Thursday, leaving millions of children increasingly exposed to disease, malnutrition and violence.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.

rfi.title: MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues

rfi.title: Corruption in Kenya taking massive toll on economic growth, warns World Bank

lemonde.description: Le sélectionneur des Bleus a retenu 23 joueurs pour les prochaines rencontres de la France, en Italie et contre la Turquie. Pablo Pagis a été retenu pour la première fois, tandis que Marcus Thuram fait son retour dans le groupe.

france24fr.title: Après les élections de mi-mandat : l'économie américaine à l'heure des comptes
france24fr.description: La déroute du camp Trump aux États-Unis est-elle d’abord celle de sa politique économique ? Au début de son second mandat, le président américain Donald Trump promettait un nouvel âge d'or et se posait en champion du pouvoir d'achat.

france24fr.title: Nouvelle liste des Bleus : Mbappé et Tchouaméni de retour, première convocation pour Pablo Pagis
france24fr.description: Zinédine Zidane a dévoilé, vendredi, la nouvelle liste de joueurs de l'Équipe de France qui disputeront les matchs pour accéder aux quarts de final de la Ligue des nations, face à la Turquie et l'Italie. On y retrouve notamment Kylian Mbappé et Aurélien Tchouameni, remis de leurs blessures. Pablo Pagis, attaquant du Paris FC, a été convoqué pour la première fois.

france24fr.title: Vols menacés : les fausses alertes à la bombe, une arme redoutable pour la guerre hybride ?
france24fr.description: La multiplication des fausses alertes à la bombe a créé de la confusion à travers toute l’Europe. Ces incidents ressemblent à de nouveaux épisodes de la guerre hybride menée par certains États comme la Russie en Europe, mais rien ne permet d’accuser formellement Moscou. Et puis, il y a cette étrange revendication des "combattants de l’État masculin", un groupuscule masculiniste qui semble lié à un obscur réseau d’extrême droite russe...

france24fr.title: Midterms aux États-Unis : Trump dénonce des "élections truquées" sans avancer de preuve
france24fr.description: Lors d’un échange avec des journalistes à la Maison-Blanche ce jeudi 5 novembre, Donald Trump a assuré que les élections aux États-Unis étaient "truquées".

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Quatre questions à Clarisse Agbegnenou, athlète modèle des Jeux
france24fr.description: À l'occasion des Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse 2026 qui se déroulent à Dakar, le Comité international olympique a proposé à la judokate Clarisse Agbengenou d'être athlète modèle. Un rôle qu'elle a accepté avec plaisir dans le but d'encourager, d'encadrer et de donner des conseils aux jeunes athlètes de haut niveau.

france24fr.title: La mobilisation lycéenne fait école en Europe : l'Union européenne face aux colères sociales
france24fr.description: L'Europe est en pleine ébullition sociale. À l'instar de la France, d'où sont partis les premiers mouvements lycéens, plusieurs pays de l'Union font face à des vagues de contestation dans la rue. L'Italie, la Belgique, la Grèce ou encore l'Allemagne connaissent des manifestations de plus ou moins grande ampleur.

france24fr.title: 11-Novembre à l'école : l'obligation de commémorer divise les enseignants
france24fr.description: Le ministère de l'Éducation nationale a instauré, pour le 11-Novembre, une nouvelle cérémonie obligatoire dans tous les établissements scolaires à partir du CM1, en hommage à tous les "morts pour la France". Certains syndicats s'y opposent et appellent au boycott, dénonçant une "glorification de la guerre".

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot évoque des "progrès importants" dans les discussions pour former un gouvernement
france24fr.description: Le centriste Gadi Eisenkot, adversaire de Benjamin Netanyahu, fait état vendredi de "progrès importants" dans les discussions pour former le prochain gouvernement israélien après les élections législatives. La veille, il avait annoncé avoir obtenu le soutien notoire de la principale liste arabe.

france24fr.title: La COP31 en Turquie s'ouvrira avec peu d'attentes de la part de l'Union européenne
france24fr.description: La COP31, qui s'ouvrira lundi 9 novembre à Antalya en Turquie, suscite peu d'attentes chez les Européens. La Commission européenne a expliqué vendredi ne pas s'attendre à une "révolution" en matière de climat, mais espère néanmoins des progrès concrets en matière d'énergies propres.

france24fr.title: Vague démocrate aux élections de mi-mandat : et maintenant ?
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont connu un véritable tsunami il y a quelques jours, ou plutôt un "Bluenami" pour reprendre l'expression consacrée. Car c'est bien une déferlante bleue qui a submergé le Capitole mardi dernier lors des élections de mi-mandat – une vague démocrate qui a balayé les républicains. Pour nous aider à décrypter cet épisode inédit de l'histoire politique américaine, notre invité : Hugo Toudic, docteur en philosophie politique et spécialiste des institutions américaines.

france24fr.title: Une organisation de colons extrémistes israéliens a établi un avant-poste à quelques kilomètres de Gaza
france24fr.description: Depuis trois semaines, le mouvement de colonisation extrémiste Nachala a installé un campement temporaire  dans la forêt de Simhoni, à trois kilomètres de la bande de Gaza, avec pour objectif d’entrer dans l’enclave palestinienne. Leur sort pourrait dépendre du prochain gouvernement qui se formera à la suite des élections législatives du 27 octobre.

france24fr.title: Tourisme en Nouvelle-Calédonie : des tour-opérateurs sur place
france24fr.description: Des tour-opérateurs australiens, néo-zélandais et français sont actuellement dans le nord de la Nouvelle-Calédonie – à Hienghène et Poindimié –, deux destinations authentiques et culturelles. Leur objectif : découvrir les richesses du Caillou et promouvoir la destination dans leur catalogue. De quoi booster l'économie en berne depuis les émeutes de 2024 qui avaient secoué l'archipel.

france24fr.title: Un Indien sauve, seul, son île de l'érosion en plantant une forêt à main nues
france24fr.description: En Inde, un agriculteur sauve son île de l'érosion en plantant, seul, une forêt à main nues. Baptisé "Forest Man", Jadav Payeng a consacré plus de 40 ans de sa vie à mettre en terre des arbres un par un sur son île, menacée par l'érosion. Aujourd'hui, la forêt porte son nom et s'étend sur plus de 500 hectares.

france24fr.title: Cyberattaques : quand le monde réel sera ciblé par des agents IA en essaim
france24fr.description: Des chambres froides contenant du plasma sanguin reprogrammées à 110 degrés, une banque française victime d'un détournement de près de 100 millions d'euros, des supermarchés européens piratés à distance... En cette première semaine de novembre 2026, les cyberattaques menacent désormais nos infrastructures vitales.

france24fr.title: Alertes à la bombe : le ciel européen sous tension
france24fr.description: Une série de fausses alertes à la bombe agite l'Europe vendredi, après des dizaines d'alertes similaires cette semaine, visant des vols commerciaux mais aussi des médias et mobilisant les forces de sécurité. Les précisions de Michel Polacco, journaliste spécialiste du secteur aéronautique et spatial.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation lycéenne : le gouvernement est "six semaines en retard" selon Philippe Aghion
france24fr.description: "On aurait pu éviter le 17 octobre", assure l'économise Philippe Aghion, ancien conseiller d'Emmanuel Macron. Au micro d'"Avec Judith", le prix Nobel d'économie 2025 présente sa vision de l'innovation comme moteur principal de la croissance économique. Retrouvez le podcast dans son intégralité ce samedi midi sur la chaîne YouTube de France 24.

france24fr.title: Charlotte Gainsbourg est Gisèle Halimi
france24fr.description: Sonia Patricelli et Thomas Baurez évoquent les sorties cinéma de la semaine. Ils débutent avec le film événement "L'Affaire Marie-Claire", inspiré du procès dit de Bobigny. En 1972, l'avocate féministe Gisèle Halimi avait défendu une jeune fille, victime d'un viol, qui avait avorté. Un "crime" dans la France de 1972. Charlotte Gainsbourg campe la célèbre pénaliste, décédée en 2020.

france24fr.title: Espace aérien : une nouvelle vague de fausses alertes à la bombe agite l'Europe
france24fr.description: Une série de fausses alertes à la bombe agite l'Europe vendredi, après des dizaines d'alertes similaires cette semaine, visant des vols commerciaux mais aussi des médias et mobilisant les forces de sécurité.

zeit.title: Dax: Dax fällt tief, US-Börsen erholen sich
zeit.description: Der Deutsche Aktienindex ist nach seinem Allzeithoch unter 26.000 Punkte gerutscht. Die US-Börsen erholten sich dagegen von ihren Kursrückgängen im Halbleitersektor.

zeit.description: Die Ukraine und Russland verhandeln wieder, Trump kündigt ein Abkommen für »ganz Europa« an. Das erinnert an Russlands Ultimatum vor dem Krieg. Der Wochenrückblick

zeit.title: EZB-Nachfolge: Zwei Bewerber für das Präsidialamt der EZB nominiert
zeit.description: Die Niederlande und Spanien haben jeweils Nominierungen für den Präsidentenposten der Europäischen Zentralbank abgegeben. Christine Lagarde verlässt das Amt frühzeitig.

zeit.title: Gleichstellung an Hochschulen: »Der Gegenwind wird größer«
zeit.description: Die AfD will Gleichstellungsprogramme an den Universitäten stoppen. Kann eine »Wissenschafts-Nato« dagegen helfen?

zeit.description: 60 deutsche Medaillengewinner der Maccabiah 2026 waren am Freitag im Berliner Kanzleramt zu Gast.

Stiefväter: War Ihr Stiefvater der bessere Vater?
zeit.description: Stiefväter haben wie Stiefmütter einen schlechten Ruf. Dabei sind sie manchmal die verlässlicheren Väter. Erzählen Sie uns von Ihren Erfahrungen.

Demonstrierende besetzen KI-Baustelle in Amsterdam

zeit.description: José Manuel Albares wertet die jüngsten Flugzeugbombendrohungen als Angriff auf Europa. Er spricht vom »Versuch hybrider Aggression und psychologischer Kriegsführung«.

zeit.title: Ilse Aigner: CDU und CSU wollen Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin
zeit.description: Die unionsinterne Debatte um die Nachfolge von Frank-Walter Steinmeier ist beendet. Die CDU will die CSU-Politikerin Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin nominieren.

observador.title: Macau a caminho de novo mínimo histórico de nascimentos
observador.description: Menos 93 nascimentos do que no mesmo período de 2025. A taxa de fecundidade de Macau cai há 11 anos consecutivos e está muito aquém dos 2,1 necessários para substituir gerações.

observador.title: Fenprof acusa Governo de atropelo à negociação
observador.description: Diploma aprovado em Conselho de Ministros permite contratar licenciados sem formação pedagógica para o 1.º ciclo. Sindicato diz que negociação foi "uma encenação".

observador.title: Governo quer combater condução com álcool e droga
observador.description: Governo quer reduzir em 50% as mortes e feridos graves nas estradas portuguesas até 2030, o que significa passar de 626 para 313 mortos e de 2.089 para 1.044 feridos graves por ano.

observador.title: Barragens. EDP deu garantia para suspender execução fiscal
observador.description: Elétrica confirma que recebeu liquidações de IRC e Imposto de Selo por conta da venda de seis barragens, sem revelar valores. E diz que apresentou garantia bancária para suspender execução fiscal.

observador.title: Amadora mantém taxa mínima de IMI nos prédios urbanos
observador.description: A proposta dos socialistas fixa as taxas do IMI em 0,8% para os prédios rústicos e 0,3% nos prédios urbanos. A medida foi aprovada com votos a favor do PS, do PSD e do Chega e abstenção da CDU.

observador.title: Isaltino Morais:  "Os moderados não têm onde votar"
observador.description: Contactado por militantes do PSD, PS e CDS-PP, o presidente da Câmara de Oeiras defende uma força que obrigue os dois maiores partidos a "entenderem-se".

observador.title: Princípe Harry e Elton John recorrem contra o Daily Mail
observador.description: Queixosos garantem que grupo de media onde se inclui o Daily Mail escutava os telefones de figuras públicas para recolher informação ilegalmente. No verão, juiz não lhes deu razão.

observador.title: Autarquias recebem 477 imóveis públicos para habitação
observador.description: Além da lista feita pela Estamo, as autarquias poderão ainda identificar outros bens de património imobiliário público, sem utilização, e solicitar a transferência da sua gestão.

observador.title: Programação de Natal arranca dia 28 e custa 765 mil euros
observador.description: A Câmara do Porto aumentou em 65 mil euros o investimento nas iluminações de Natal face a 2025. Dezembro traz música, teatro, dança, pista de gelo e espaço para neurodivergentes.

observador.title: Dois altos cargos marroquinos deram instruções em Ceuta
observador.description: Vídeos analisados pela polícia espanhola mostram dois responsáveis marroquinos a deram instruções aos migrantes que tentavam entrar em Espanha.

observador.title: Lisboa. Defesa dos habitantes detidos apela ao "bom senso"
observador.description: Ricardo Sá Fernandes declarou que o Ministério Público deve ser o primeiro garante dos direitos fundamentais dos cidadãos, apelando ao "bom senso". Cinco dos detidos aceitaram a suspensão provisória.

observador.title: PSD/Madeira apresenta proposta de revisão constitucional
observador.description: PSD da Madeira defende uma maior representatividade política para o parlamento regional, tendo admitido a emissão de uma posição conjunta entre parlamentos da Madeira e dos Açores.

observador.title: PCP quer passes de transportes públicos a 20 euros
observador.description: O PCP fez mais de 500 propostas de alteração ao Orçamento do Estado, sem quantificar os valores totais, porque, diz, têm de ser vistas no conjunto.

observador.title: Casa da Arquitetura e Museu Óscar Niemeyer definem parceria
observador.description: O protocolo é assinado na segunda-feira e abre porta a exposições, publicações e intercâmbio de arquitetos e investigadores entre Matosinhos e Curitiba.

observador.title: Portugal repudia condenação de Au Kam San
observador.description: MNE transmitiu às autoridades chinesas "repúdio e séria preocupação" após tribunal de Macau condenar o cidadão português por crimes contra a segurança do Estado.

observador.title: Sindicato defende aumento salarial para técnicos da AIMA
observador.description: STM critica aumento silencioso dos salários dos dirigentes da AIMA e exige o mesmo para os técnicos. OE2027 prevê dotação de 135 milhões para a agência.

observador.title: GNR interceta embarcação ligada ao narcotráfico
observador.description: A apreensão ocorreu após a GNR ter recebido uma informação sobre o "carregamento de vários jerricãs com combustível, num local isolado". Foram intercetados 3 suspeitos, e um quarto pôs-se em fuga.

spiegel.title: Tesla Cybertruck: Das war das Auto der Trump-Ära
spiegel.description: Elon Musk verabschiedet sich nach drei Jahren vom Cybertruck. Die Amerikaner haben das monströse Gefährt abgewählt, wirtschaftlich wie politisch.

spiegel.title: Demokrat Adam Hamilton: Ein Pastor aus Kansas zieht in den US-Senat
spiegel.description: Adam Hamilton predigt »radikale Liebe«. Als erster Demokrat seit 94 Jahren zieht er nun für Kansas in den US-Senat. Daheim, in seiner »Megakirche«, sorgen sich so manche um ihren Pastor. Ein Besuch.

spiegel.title: EZB: Welche Chancen Deutschland bei der Nachfolge von Christine Lagarde hat
spiegel.description: Ein Spanier oder ein Niederländer wird auf Christine Lagarde als Präsident der Europäischen Zentralbank folgen. Deutschland geht einmal mehr leer aus – und streitet mit Frankreich um weitere Topjobs bei der EZB.

spiegel.title: »Die Olchis«-Schöpfer Erhard Dietl dichtet zum Abschied von Janosch
spiegel.description: Einer der Größten der Kinderliteratur ist gestorben – und die Branche trauert. Zu Ehren Janoschs gezeichnet und geschrieben hat auch Erhard Dietl, Autor und Illustrator der Reihe über die Müllkippenbewohner »Die Olchis«.

spiegel.title: »Hamlet« im Berliner Ensemble: Ersan Mondtag verlegt den Klassiker ins heutige Deutschland
spiegel.description: Ersan Mondtag und Wilke Weermann verlegen in Berlin Shakespeares Klassiker »Hamlet« ins Deutschland von heute – und zeigen einen Theatercomic aus jugendlichem Sturm und sexuellem Drang, Drogenparanoia und Kriegsangst.

spiegel.title: NRW-Heimatministerium: Zeuge über Machtmissbrauch - »Das halten Sie als Mensch kaum aus«
spiegel.description: Eine Arbeitsatmosphäre voll »Angst und Schrecken«? Im Untersuchungsausschuss spricht der Kronzeuge zu den Vorwürfen gegen NRW-Ministerin Scharrenbach. Es geht um Einschüchterungen, Zwietracht – und gesundheitliche Folgen.

spiegel.title: Berlinale-Skandal: Claudia Roths Eingeständnis zum Vorwurf des Antisemitismus
spiegel.description: Die ehemalige Kulturstaatsministerin bereut, die Berlinale-Preisverleihung kritisiert zu haben – und spricht von zu großem Druck. Was das über ihr Amtsverständnis enthüllt.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Warum die SPD-Spitze auf ein Scheitern von Rot-Grün-Rot hofft
spiegel.description: Die Berliner Koalitionsverhandlungen für Rot-Grün-Rot werden zur Belastung für die SPD. In der Partei setzen viele auf einen Abbruch der Gespräche. Sie sehen die sozialdemokratischen Grundwerte in Gefahr.

spiegel.title: Kenia: Sektenführer Paul Mackenzie zu 200 Jahren Haft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Seinen Anhängern predigte Paul Mackenzie, Leiden und Sterben seien der einzige Weg zu Jesus. Fast 200 Menschen starben, viele verhungerten, darunter auch Neugeborene und Kleinkinder. Reue zeigte er offenbar nicht.

spiegel.title: Midterms: Iowas neuer Gouverneur Rob Sand glitt früher für Prada über den Laufsteg
spiegel.description: Demokrat Rob Sand hat sich bei der Wahl in Iowa überraschend durchgesetzt. Ähnlich gut lief es für ihn offenbar während eines früheren Nebenjobs.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Börsenbeben an der Wall Street, AfD-Hacker, Vanessa Emde droht Parteiausschluss
spiegel.description: Der Demokratensieg bei den US-Zwischenwahlen verunsichert die Börsen. Die Spur der AfD-Hacker führt in eine berüchtigte Onlineszene. Die Berliner Linkenspitze will endlich Vanessa Emde loswerden. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Thomas Markle: Vater von Meghan Markle wegen mutmaßlichem Besitz von Kindesmissbrauchsbildern festgenommen
spiegel.description: Missbrauchsvorwürfe gegen Thomas Markle beschäftigen die Behörden. Ermittler durchsuchten sein früheres Wohnhaus auf den Philippinen. Nun wurde der Vater von Herzogin Meghan in den USA angeklagt.

spiegel.title: »Königreich Deutschland«: Prozessauftakt gegen Fantasiekönig Peter Fitzek
spiegel.description: Er nannte sich König, die Untertanen zahlten. Nun sitzt Peter Fitzek vor dem Oberlandesgericht Düsseldorf. Dort stellt sich die Frage, was das »Königreich Deutschland« war: Geschäftsmodell oder staatsfeindlicher Wahn?

spiegel.title: Deutsche Welle: Belarus schreibt DW-Journalistinnen zur Fahndung aus
spiegel.description: Seit April 2024 hat Belarus die Deutsche Welle als »extremistische Organisation« eingestuft. Nun fahndet der autoritär regierte Staat nach vier Mitarbeiterinnen des deutschen Medienanbieters – wie auch Russland.

spiegel.title: Hakeem Jeffries (Demokraten): Der Gegenspieler von Donald Trump im neuen Kongress
spiegel.description: Hakeem Jeffries soll als Sprecher des Repräsentantenhauses das dritthöchste Amt der USA bekleiden. Weniger klar ist, wer demokratischer Mehrheitsführer im Senat wird. Sicher ist nur: Für Donald Trump wird es ungemütlich.

spiegel.title: Bombendrohungen gegen Flugzeuge: Was bisher bekannt ist und wie Piloten, Flugsicherung und Behörden darauf vorbereitet sind
spiegel.description: Mindestens 30 Bombendrohungen gegen Flugzeuge in ganz Europa: Wie Flugsicherung und Bundespolizei reagieren – und wie Piloten auf solche Situationen vorbereitet sind.

spiegel.title: A2: Zwei Menschen sterben bei Absturz von Kleinflugzeug nordöstlich von Magdeburg
spiegel.description: Das Unglück ereignete sich nahe dem Autobahnparkplatz Krähenberge: Ein Kleinflugzeug ist auf die A2 gestürzt, zwei Insassen starben dabei.

spiegel.title: Gefahren im Gebirge: Selbstüberschätzung und Vollkaskomentalität am Berg
spiegel.description: Bergsport boomt, es wagen sich aber auch immer mehr Menschen ohne Vorkenntnisse in ungewohntes Terrain. Hier spricht Thomas Wanner vom Alpenverein über den heiklen Trend, Ausflüge mit ChatGPT zu planen.

In the lab, scientists have long put enzymes to work making useful chemicals. But nature's enzymes cannot do every reaction a researcher might want. Sometimes scientists need an enzyme to take on a job it did not evolve to do. That's where enzyme engineering comes in—researchers make changes to an enzyme, test how those changes affect what the enzyme does and look for version

phys-org.title: 'I heard a barnacle'—how paying attention to nature's background noise can reveal animal secrets
phys-org.description: During four days on Washington's Olympic Peninsula, I saw an Olympic marmot, a species found nowhere else on Earth; four bumblebee species working the same lavender plant; three western hermit crab species new to me; and five orcas slicing through the dark water off Ediz Hook. Any one of them could have been the trip's highlight.

phys-org.title: Vibrating mirrors of light create analog of a black hole event horizon
phys-org.description: Optical cavities are pairs of light-trapping mirrors and underpin the operation of lasers, atomic clocks and many types of precision sensors. If the distance between the mirrors is changed rapidly enough, some theories predict that the waves inside them should bunch together into short, intense pulses. So far, however, this prediction has never been tested directly.

phys-org.title: The John Lewis Christmas ad captures the deep need for grandmothers
phys-org.description: Like many of us, I always enjoy the John Lewis Christmas ad and 2026 is no different. This year, I love the fact that the star of the show is a grandmother.

phys-org.description: Penn State researchers have refined an atom-scale model of how silicon carbide changes from a solid into vapor during crystal growth, work that could help manufacturers produce higher-quality material for advanced electronics while reducing costly trial-and-error experiments.

phys-org.title: States tax sports betting heavily, but gamblers may barely feel it
phys-org.description: Sports betting has grown explosively since 2018, when a U.S. Supreme Court ruling struck down a federal ban on it. Now, Americans wager more than $165 billion on sports annually, contributing to an industry larger than state-run lotteries even excluding prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket.

phys-org.title: Scientists achieve record-breaking low temperature on China's space station, paving the way for new physics experiments
phys-org.description: Matter starts to behave differently at extremely low temperatures, creating conditions ideal for studying quantum physics and new states of matter. Now, researchers from China have achieved a new low-temperature record aboard their Tiangong space station. Their research, recently published in Science, might lead to a new generation of experiments in quantum physics and precision measurements in space.

phys-org.title: Evolutionary history and genetic basis of spruce diversification revealed
phys-org.description: The genus Picea (spruce) is widely distributed across the Northern Hemisphere and is a dominant component of boreal and montane forests. Understanding the evolutionary processes that have shaped diversification and regional differentiation across the genus requires a well-resolved phylogeny of Picea. However, the evolutionary history of Picea has long been obscure due to conflicting genetic signals.

phys-org.title: Researchers establish G0 founder population carrying targeted mutations in marine mollusks
phys-org.description: Although genome-editing-based breeding has advanced rapidly in aquaculture, progress in marine mollusks has lagged behind. The main challenge is not genome editing itself, but rather rearing the few edited larvae through metamorphosis to establish a viable G0 founder population.

phys-org.title: Technique that spots tRNAs in action could accelerate drug development for inherited diseases
phys-org.description: Human cells turn genetic instructions into proteins with great precision. Critical for the translation of this information are transfer RNAs, or tRNAs, small molecules that read the genetic code three letters at a time and bring the matching building blocks of proteins, the amino acids, to the cell's protein-making machinery, the ribosome.

phys-org.title: New method for upcycling polyethylene is suitable for mass production as a raw material for nylon
phys-org.description: It would greatly benefit the environment and climate if nylon—chemically known as polyamide—could be produced on a large scale from plastic waste in the future, rather than from petroleum, as has been the norm until now. At LIKAT in Rostock, chemists pursuing this approach have succeeded in selectively converting polyethylene—the main component of all plastic waste—into dicarboxylic acids, which can serve as chemical precursors for nylon.

phys-org.title: Robot successfully builds space structure in first autonomous construction demo
phys-org.description: A robotic truss builder that was conceived, designed and built by Caltech researchers has successfully built a structure in space—without the help of astronauts—for the first time. The truss builder, part of DARPA's Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D) program, consists of an autonomous manipulator that picks up struts and joints held in nearby dispensers to repeatedly assemble identical sections, or bays, of a perimeter truss.

phys-org.title: New 3D microscope packs many imaging tools into one system
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers led by UT Southwestern Medical Center has developed a versatile light-sheet microscope that captures 3D views of biological samples, from activity inside living cells to larger tissues. Designed to make detailed imaging much simpler and faster, the approach could help laboratories stretch equipment budgets and expand research that may ultimately inform patient care.

phys-org.title: World-first successful wild release of endangered broad-headed snake
phys-org.description: The broad-headed snake (Hoplocephalus bungaroides), one of Australia's most endangered snakes, has been given a lifeline, with at least four of six captive-bred juveniles surviving the critical first few months after their release into the wild.

phys-org.title: Tiny biodegradable particles poke openings in skin to boost topical drug delivery
phys-org.description: Skin is remarkably good at keeping things out of the body. Typically, that's a positive. It becomes an issue when medicine needs to get in. Swallow a pill to treat a skin condition, and the medicine enters your stomach, moves into your bloodstream and travels throughout your body—all to reach a problem in your skin.

phys-org.title: Oh boy, all girls again: Research tracks sea turtle sex ratios
phys-org.description: Forty young sea turtles recently reached an important milestone at Florida Atlantic University: They were finally big enough to leave the university's marine science laboratory and return to the ocean. Their release was a reason to celebrate. But for FAU researchers who have spent years studying loggerhead, leatherback and green sea turtle hatchlings, there is a growing concern about what the next generation of sea turtles may look like: They're almost all girls.

phys-org.title: How foreign investment can strengthen African governments' control over land
phys-org.description: African governments are using foreign investment, infrastructure projects and conservation schemes to extend their control over land and communities, according to new research spanning 14 countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

phys-org.title: Microplastic pollution could be changing the color of the Pacific Ocean
phys-org.description: Our oceans have effectively become trash dumps where massive quantities of plastic end up. So much so, in fact, that the largest offshore plastic accumulation zone has been labeled the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who's Winning (and Who's Losing) The Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.
